sources.citation: Amin, Muhammad & Zahid Ali. 2021. Phonological and Morphological Variations between Lasi and Standard Sindhi. Horizon Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences Research 3(2): 181-194. DOI 10.37534/bp.jhssr.2021.v3.n2.id1109.p181.

sources.note: Nothing about Lasi stress. Segmental variation only (r/l addition, loss of breathy voicing, v > b/implosive, t-deletion, palatalization, insertion, deletion, lexical differences). 'stress' occurs 4 times, all in the literature review on Rotuman/loanword metathesis (pp. 184-185).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1919. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VIII Part I: Indo-Aryan Family, North-Western Group: Specimens of the Sindhi and Lahnda. Calcutta. 'Lasi' section pp. 158-161 (+ word list pp. 214ff.).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Lasi section (pp. 158-161) covers only contraction, final short-vowel dropping, disaspiration, noun/pronoun forms and the verb substantive; p. 158: 'Lasi differs but little from Standard Sindhi.' A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole volume for accent/stress finds only the general transliteration note and remarks on other languages; nothing for Sindhi or Lasi.

sources.note: The only explicit word-stress rule for Sindhi (heavy-syllable based); Grierson says Lasi differs little from Standard Sindhi, so this is the default rule a Lasi statement would be measured against. Only Google Books snippets are held (sind1272).
